name: OMTech 90W CO₂
tagline: Cabinet CO₂ with a 500 × 700 mm bed, 90W glass tube and four-way pass-through
tldr: OMTech now sells its 500 × 700 mm cabinet laser with a 90W Yongli H2 glass tube, under model numbers that still end in -80: the MF2028-80 with manual focus ($2,999.99) and the AF2028-80 with motorized autofocus on a taller stand ($3,299.99). Both have a Ruida control panel, USB and Ethernet, front, rear and side pass-through doors, air assist and an exhaust fan built in. Cooling is a pump and tank in the base package; a 6 L chiller costs $500 more. It replaces our OMTech 80W profile. No independent review of the 90W version yet.
mainObjective: Production cutting of acrylic and wood on a 500 × 700 mm bed in a workshop, for the price of a large desktop CO₂

priceRange.note: Official OMTech store, Oct 2026: MF2028-80 (manual focus) $2,999.99, AF2028-80 (autofocus) $3,299.99; chiller, LightBurn and rotary bundles up to $3,999.99 (MF) and $4,299.99 (AF)

pros: 90W tube and 500 × 700 mm bed from $2,999.99 (OMTech, Oct 2026): more power and area per dollar than desktop CO₂ machines
Front, rear and side pass-through doors (835 × 95 mm and 520 × 20 mm) for sheets longer than the bed
Ruida control panel with USB, Ethernet and offline jobs from a flash drive, supported by LightBurn
cons: The base package cools the tube with a pump and tank; a 6 L chiller adds $500 and is worth it for long runs
No camera, and manual focus on the MF2028-80; autofocus needs the AF2028-80 at $300 more
103 to 117 kg and about 1.5 m long: it needs a workshop floor, a 110 V outlet and an outside vent

faq.question: Why is a 90W laser called MF2028-80?
faq.answer: OMTech kept the old model numbers when it fitted a 90W Yongli H2 tube to the 500 × 700 mm cabinet machines, around early 2025 according to archived store pages. The MF2028-80 and AF2028-80 sold today are the 90W machines; used units listed as 80W usually have the older 80W tube.

faq.question: MF2028-80 or AF2028-80: which one should I buy?
faq.answer: Both share the 90W tube, the 500 × 700 mm bed, the controller and the pass-through doors. The AF2028-80 adds motorized autofocus and stands on a taller frame (930 mm high instead of 680 mm). If you change material thickness often, the $300 difference pays for itself in setup time; for long runs of the same sheet, the MF2028-80 is enough.

faq.question: Do I need the water chiller package?
faq.answer: The standard package includes a submersible pump and a tank, and OMTech asks for distilled water between 16 and 21 °C. That works for short jobs in a cool room. For daily production or a warm workshop, a chiller keeps the tube in range and protects its life; the chiller package costs $500 more than the standard one.

standoutFeatures.title: 90W on a 500 × 700 mm bed for about $3,000
standoutFeatures.body: The MF2028-80 pairs a 90W glass tube with a 500 × 700 mm bed for $2,999.99 on OMTech's store in October 2026, less than OMTech's own Polar 2 desktop machines with a smaller bed and tube.

standoutFeatures.title: Four-way pass-through
standoutFeatures.body: Front and rear doors open an 835 × 95 mm slot and side doors a 520 × 20 mm slot, so long sheets and panels can be worked in sections.

standoutFeatures.title: Ruida controller with offline jobs
standoutFeatures.body: The control panel frames, pauses and runs files from a flash drive without a computer, and connects by USB or Ethernet. LightBurn supports it on Windows and macOS; the bundled RDWorks runs on Windows only.

beginnerNotes: This profile covers the 90W machines OMTech sells today under the MF2028-80 and AF2028-80 names. It is a workshop machine, not a desktop one: plan floor space, a 110 V circuit, distilled water or a chiller, and a duct to the outside before it arrives. Budget for LightBurn if you work on a Mac.
proTips: Keep routine cuts under about 70% power: OMTech rates the tube at 7,000–8,000 hours at 10–40% but 3,000–4,000 hours at 70–100%. Check the mirror alignment after delivery and after any move, starting from the first mirror. Clean the lens and mirrors weekly in production, and keep a spare lens on the shelf.

editorialDepth.advantages: The 90W OMTech gives a sign shop or a growing business a 500 × 700 mm bed, real pass-through doors and enough power for 9–10 mm acrylic, for about the price of a large desktop CO₂. The Ruida controller is a known quantity: LightBurn supports it, jobs run offline from a flash drive, and spare tubes, lenses and mirrors are easy to find.
editorialDepth.limitations: It is a heavy cabinet that needs a workshop, an outside vent and proper cooling: the pump and tank of the base package are a minimum, not a production setup. There is no camera, autofocus costs extra, and the glass tube is a consumable with a one-year warranty. Figures are OMTech's until independent reviews of the 90W version appear.
